title: Mitigating Social Desirability Bias in Random Silicon Sampling
findings: The sensitivity of simulated survey responses for the 'church attendance' demographic to different prompt mitigation strategies is consistent with patterns observed in other demographic groups. This suggests that biases in simulation are not driven by any single demographic axis like religion, but rather reflect broader structural properties of how LLMs emulate population-conditioned responses.
